prompt: Why are tetrahydrofuran and dioxane often used as solvents?

choices.text: They are generally inert, although strong acids can cleave them
They are strained rings that react readily with most reagents
choices.why: That describes epoxides. Tetrahydrofuran and dioxane behave like open-chain ethers and are fairly inert.

choices.text: They can't be cleaved by any reagent, not even strong acids
choices.why: Like other ethers, they can be cleaved by strong acids.

choices.text: Their ring oxygens make them strongly acidic
choices.why: Ether oxygens have no acidic hydrogen. These solvents are chosen for their inertness.

explanation: For the most part, cyclic ethers behave like acyclic ethers. Common cyclic ethers such as tetrahydrofuran and dioxane are often used as solvents because of their inertness, yet they can be cleaved by strong acids.

prompt: How many atoms make up the ring of an epoxide (an oxirane)?
explanation: Epoxides, or oxiranes, are three-membered cyclic ethers: two carbons and one oxygen in the ring. The strain of the three-membered ring gives epoxides unique chemical reactivity.

prompt: Which cyclic ethers behave differently from open-chain ethers, and why?

choices.text: Epoxides, because of the strain of their three-membered ring
Tetrahydrofurans, because of the strain of their five-membered ring
choices.why: Tetrahydrofuran behaves like an open-chain ether and is used as an inert solvent.

choices.text: Dioxanes, because their two ring oxygens make them strongly acidic
choices.why: Dioxane behaves like an open-chain ether and is used as an inert solvent.

choices.text: Epoxides, because their ring oxygen carries an O–H group
choices.why: An epoxide oxygen has no O–H group. Its special reactivity comes from ring strain.

explanation: The one group of cyclic ethers that behaves differently from open-chain ethers is the three-membered-ring compounds called epoxides, or oxiranes. The strain of the three-membered ring gives epoxides unique chemical reactivity.

prompt: Approximately how much ethylene oxide is produced worldwide each year, in millions of tons?
explanation: Approximately 37 million tons of ethylene oxide is produced worldwide each year, most of it by air oxidation of ethylene over a silver oxide catalyst at 300 °C.

prompt: How is most ethylene oxide made industrially?

choices.text: By air oxidation of ethylene over a silver oxide catalyst at 300 °C
By treating ethylene with m-chloroperoxybenzoic acid
choices.why: Peroxyacids are the usual laboratory method for epoxides, not the industrial route to ethylene oxide.

choices.text: By treating a halohydrin made from ethylene with base
choices.why: Most ethylene oxide is made by air oxidation of ethylene over a silver oxide catalyst.

choices.text: By dehydrating ethylene glycol with sulfuric acid
choices.why: Ethylene glycol is made from ethylene oxide, not the other way round.

explanation: Most ethylene oxide is made by air oxidation of ethylene over a silver oxide catalyst at 300 °C. This process is not useful for other epoxides, however, and is of little value in the laboratory.

prompt: What is the systematic name for ethylene oxide?

choices.text: 1,2-Epoxyethane
1,2-Epoxyethene
choices.why: The -ene ending implies a double bond, which ethylene oxide doesn't have. That's exactly why the name ethylene oxide isn't systematic.

choices.text: 1,2-Epoxypropane
choices.why: Ethylene oxide has two carbons; 1,2-epoxypropane has three.

choices.text: Ethylene glycol
choices.why: Ethylene glycol is a diol made from ethylene oxide, not another name for it.

explanation: The name ethylene oxide is not systematic, because the -ene ending implies a double bond in the molecule. It's used because ethylene oxide is derived from ethylene by adding an oxygen atom. The systematic name is 1,2-epoxyethane.

prompt: What is the organic product when cycloheptene reacts with m-chloroperoxybenzoic acid in dichloromethane?

choices.text: 1,2-Epoxycycloheptane
trans-1,2-Cycloheptanediol
choices.why: A diol would form only after the epoxide is opened by aqueous acid. The peroxyacid alone gives the epoxide.

choices.text: trans-2-Chlorocycloheptanol
choices.why: A chlorohydrin forms from an alkene with Cl2 and water, not with a peroxyacid.

choices.text: Cycloheptanol
choices.why: The peroxyacid adds an oxygen atom across the double bond to form a three-membered ring, not an alcohol.

explanation: In the laboratory, epoxides are usually prepared by treating an alkene with a peroxyacid (RCO3H), typically m-chloroperoxybenzoic acid. Cycloheptene gives 1,2-epoxycycloheptane, along with m-chlorobenzoic acid as the by-product.

prompt: Cyclohexene reacts with Cl2 and water to give trans-2-chlorocyclohexanol. Treating this halohydrin with NaOH gives 1,2-epoxycyclohexane. What kind of reaction forms the epoxide?

choices.text: An intramolecular Williamson ether synthesis
An E1 dehydration of the alcohol
choices.why: No carbocation forms. Under basic conditions the alkoxide oxygen displaces chloride within the same molecule.

choices.text: An epoxidation by a peroxyacid
choices.why: No peroxyacid is used; the oxygen already in the molecule closes the ring.

choices.text: An acid-catalyzed S_N1 substitution
choices.why: The reaction uses base, and the alkoxide ion and alkyl halide in the same molecule react as in a Williamson synthesis.

explanation: When a halohydrin is treated with base, HX is eliminated and an epoxide forms by an intramolecular Williamson ether synthesis: the nucleophilic alkoxide ion and the electrophilic alkyl halide are in the same molecule.

prompt: What is the product when trans-2-butene reacts with m-chloroperoxybenzoic acid?

choices.text: trans-2,3-Epoxybutane
cis-2,3-Epoxybutane
choices.why: The cis epoxide comes from cis-2-butene. Each alkene keeps its geometry in the epoxide.

choices.text: 1,2-Epoxybutane
choices.why: The oxygen adds across the original double bond, which is between carbons 2 and 3.

choices.text: A mixture of cis- and trans-2,3-epoxybutane
choices.why: cis- and trans-2-butene give different epoxides, so the trans alkene gives only the trans epoxide.

explanation: Epoxidation keeps the geometry of the alkene: trans-2-butene gives trans-2,3-epoxybutane, while cis-2-butene gives cis-2,3-epoxybutane (Exercises 18.4.1 and 18.4.2).

prompt: Ethylene oxide is an intermediate in the manufacture of which products?

choices.text: Ethylene glycol (for antifreeze) and polyester polymers
Diethyl ether and other ether solvents
choices.why: Diethyl ether is made from ethanol and sulfuric acid (Section 18.2). Ethylene oxide is used to make ethylene glycol and polyesters.

choices.text: Ethylene and other alkenes
choices.why: Ethylene oxide is made from ethylene, not the other way round.

choices.text: m-Chloroperoxybenzoic acid and other peroxyacids
choices.why: Peroxyacids are reagents used to make epoxides, not products made from ethylene oxide.

explanation: Ethylene oxide, the simplest epoxide, is an intermediate in the manufacture of both ethylene glycol, used for automobile antifreeze, and polyester polymers.
